name: phmmer
compares: Amino-acid letters, one query protein against each protein of the relative, scored with a substitution matrix the way BLAST does but with HMMER's model of insertions and deletions.
reference: The relative's proteome (Quest for Orthologs reference proteomes, release 2020_04), as a FASTA file.
score: Domain bit score: higher ranks first. The E-value cutoff was 10.
failure_modes: Failure modes specific to phmmer: not measured in this run.

cost_per_1000_queries.hardware: Stanford Sherlock, SLURM partition hns; searches on CPU only

questions: Is the closest same-family domain in the relative you will search at least 40% identical, for most of your proteins? If yes, Fmax here is 40–60% 0.252 (n = 563), 60–100% 0.308 (n = 1,289). If no, 20–30% 0.359 (n = 93), 30–40% 0.199 (n = 165). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (430 Mya) as the relative searched, setting `default`; strata with at least 30 true instances.)

Are the features you care about longer than 60 residues? If yes, Fmax here is 61–120 aa 0.250 (n = 963), 121–250 aa 0.329 (n = 504), 251 aa or more 0.477 (n = 277). If no, 16–30 aa 0.042 (n = 271), 31–60 aa 0.095 (n = 420). (Pfam truth set, raw calls, zebrafish (430 Mya) as the relative searched, setting `default`.)
Can you spend about 0.381 CPU-hours per 1,000 proteins for each relative you search? That is the measured cost against zebrafish; the range over relatives is under "Cost per 1,000 queries" above.
